value.residual: Lean proves exact replay is state-preserving, conflicting replay rejects, and a stored receipt blocks a second abstract commit. Retained InMemory receipts bind both the semantic input hash and a canonical authority-effect digest; request-local correlation IDs are normalized out while deterministic action/ledger IDs make lost-reply reconstruction stable. Turso-persisted receipt and reopen evidence was removed in #2764 (not currently covered). The correspondence is not machine-proved, pre-v3 receipts fail closed on replay, and legacy unversioned callers remain. Public scope excludes the former engine/provider implementation and its evidence; no correspondence is claimed for that omitted code. #718 K-C: the cell kernel's idempotency decision (crates/norn-kernel/src/replay_decision.rs, called by action_commit's replay) is proved against the extracted production code (Charon/Aeneas) for every input; the claim stays reference_proved until #969: an empty key runs the call, a key holding the same call (action, object, input, actor, writer binding) replays exactly the recorded call, and any other or unreadable record is a conflict. Record decoding, the RecordedCall glue and the callers' early return before commit are trusted (TRUST-KERNEL-BINDING-GLUE); this fragment does not promote the claim.
